text:
carol_support: Customer (Acme Payments) reporting repeated 429 + 503 from Dedicated ap-southeast-2; started ~08:10 UTC, high error rate. They say autoscale didn't provision extra GPUs.

emma_csm: Customer says latency spikes to >3s/token and then 429 on burst traffic, billing meter shows normal usage but observed failures.

carol_support: Attaching quick repro they ran (trimmed token):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/generate \
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED\" \
 -d '{"model":"rw-large", "input":"test", "max_tokens":512}'
```

alice_sre: I see correlated placement failures in control-plane: \"no_available_instance_match\" for ap-southeast-2. Autoscaler attempted 2 launches -> cloud returned InsufficientHostCapacity.

bob_infra: Confirmed: cloud provider returned InsufficientHostCapacity for GPU family (a100). Autoscaler retried but hit account vGPU quota limits; no new nodes spun up.

dave_oncall: Any signs of a noisy neighbor or single-tenant saturation on that AZ?

alice_sre: Yes — one allocation (team-ml-models) is pegging 100% GPU memory and sustained 95% SM utilization across the rack. We had throttled them last night but looks like they ramped again.

emma_csm: Customer is asking for failover to us-west-2 — is cross-region failover possible for Dedicated? Risk to data locality?

bob_infra: We have a manual cross-region fallback for Dedicated (not automatic) because of data locality/KMS. We can move placement to us-west-2 if customer approves.

carol_support: Sent customer steps and asked for permission to initiate manual failover. They approved.

dave_oncall: Short-term mitigation: apply tenant-level rate-limit to the noisy tenant, reduce their batch_size, and enable model-variant fallback (quantized rw-medium) for affected customers to reduce GPU pressure.

alice_sre: Pasting scheduler logs excerpt:
```text
ERROR placement: allocate_failed: InsufficientHostCapacity (region ap-southeast-2) instance_type=gpu-a100 attempted=3
WARN autoscaler: quota_exceeded: vGPU quota for account 0/8
```

carol_support: Note — customer also reported intermittent 401s during the window which coincided with retries.

bob_infra: Those 401s look like our retry middleware misclassifying downstream failures and re-authing. I'll patch the middleware to avoid retrying on 401s so we don't double-count failures.

emma_csm: Customer agreed to a maintenance window in 30m to shift traffic to us-west-2.

dave_oncall: I'm going to apply rate-limits to the noisy tenant and kick off a small canary in us-west-2 now. @bob_infra please stand by for region move steps.

bob_infra: Executing move plan:
1) update customer's placement policy -> region: us-west-2
2) trigger placement-sync job
3) monitor token_latency and error_rate metrics
I'll post progress in ~10m.

infra-bot: [deploy] placement-sync-job started 1795123600

carol_support: Also logging a billing anomaly: customer saw duplicate meter entries during repeated retries. Filing billing ticket with finance and support tagging.

alice_sre: Tentative root cause: Insufficient host capacity in ap-southeast-2 combined with an aggressive noisy tenant saturating rack GPUs -> autoscaler couldn't recover due to cloud quota limits -> customers hit 429/503 and some retry/auth middleware surfaced 401s. Manual failover to us-west-2 mitigates.

dave_oncall: Follow-ups planned: request quota increase for ap-southeast-2, add autoscaler detection for InsufficientHostCapacity to trigger cross-region fallback earlier, implement automatic noisy-tenant throttling heuristics, and fix retry middleware.

carol_support: Customer traffic moved to us-west-2, error rates and latency returned to baseline. Closing incident but keeping monitoring alert on for 24h. :white_check_mark:
